source: NCERT Class X, Understanding Economic Development, Economics Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Production Across Countries — MNCs
points: A **Multinational Corporation (MNC)** owns or controls production in **more than one country**; it sets up production where it is **cheap and profitable** (labour, resources, markets).
MNCs invest — **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** — in assets like land, buildings, machines.
MNCs spread production by **buying local companies, forming joint ventures/partnerships**, or **placing orders** with small producers (e.g. garments, footwear) — controlling them from a distance.

sections.heading: 2. Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets
points: **Foreign trade** connects markets of different countries — giving producers a wider market and buyers more choice.
Trade **integrates markets**: prices of similar goods tend to equalise across countries.
Historically, trade routes and colonialism connected the world; today trade + investment binds economies closely.

sections.heading: 3. What is Globalisation? Its Enablers
points: **Globalisation** = the rapid **integration or interconnection between countries** through greater foreign trade and foreign investment.

sub: **Technology** — faster transport (containers, jet aircraft) and **IT/telecommunication** (internet, telephone) cut costs and delivery time.
**Liberalisation** of trade and investment policies — removing barriers/restrictions.
The **World Trade Organisation (WTO)** — aims to liberalise international trade (but rules often favour developed countries).

sections.heading: 4. Liberalisation in India and Its Impact
points: India removed **trade barriers** and started **liberalisation around 1991** — allowing free imports/exports and foreign investment.

sub: **Benefits:** greater choice, better quality, lower prices for consumers; new jobs in industries and services (IT, BPO); growth of Indian MNCs (Tata Motors, Infosys, Ranbaxy).
**Costs:** small producers/workers hurt by competition; job insecurity; uneven benefits (not fair to all).

points: **Fair globalisation** — needs government to protect workers/small producers, ensure fair WTO rules, and spread benefits widely.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: MNC = controls production in more than one country; FDI = foreign direct investment.
Globalisation = integration through trade + investment; enabled by technology + liberalisation + WTO.
WTO aims to liberalise trade, but rules often favour developed countries.
Fair globalisation = government protects workers/small producers, spreads benefits.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **FDI** = investment by MNCs (in land, buildings, machinery abroad).
**Liberalisation** = removing government barriers/restrictions on trade and investment.
The **WTO** aims to **liberalise** trade (its rules often favour rich countries).
